back: A condition caused by a diet with too little, too much or the wrong balance of nutrients.
A lack of protein in the diet, even when there is enough energy (e.g. a weaned child fed mainly on maize porridge).
Oedema (swollen feet, legs and face), swollen abdomen, peeling patchy skin, thin pale hair, poor growth.
Lack of both energy and protein (too little food). Severe wasting, loose wrinkled skin, no oedema.
Swelling caused by fluid collecting in the tissues.
notes: Seen in kwashiorkor; it is fluid, not fat.

front: Deficiency diseases of vitamin A, vitamin C, vitamin D, iron and iodine?
back: Vitamin A: night blindness. C: scurvy. D (or calcium): rickets. Iron: anaemia. Iodine: goitre.
Adding vitamins or mineral ions to everyday foods, e.g. iodine to salt.

front: How does over-eating lead to obesity?
back: Energy taken in is greater than energy used; the excess (from fat, sugar or starch) is stored as body fat.
Coronary heart disease, stroke, high blood pressure, type 2 diabetes, joint problems.
BMI = mass in kg ÷ (height in m)². Adults: 18.5–24.9 healthy, 25–29.9 overweight, 30 or more obese.

front: Why do girls and women need more iron than boys and men?
back: To replace the iron lost in blood during menstruation (and for the baby's blood in pregnancy).
